items.title: Sumitomo Life to remain cautious on JGB yields, keep investment pace unchanged from H1
items.summary: Sumitomo Life Insurance will maintain its investment pace for Japanese government bonds in the upcoming months. It intends to carefully monitor yields on super-long Japanese government bonds, assessing any market volatility. The firm expects its JGB holdings to decrease in the Asset Liability Management portfolio by the end of the fiscal year. Predictions suggest that the Bank of Japan will raise its policy rate by December.

items.title: India office market sets nine-month leasing record, with GCCs accounting for 43% of demand
items.summary: India's office market is seeing significant occupier demand with rising gross leasing figures throughout 2026. New supply and high take-up rates have resulted in a marginal increase in vacancy levels. Major cities like Mumbai and Delhi-NCR are experiencing historically low vacancy rates in prime office districts. Global Capability Centres are leading leasing activity, contributing significantly to the overall demand for office space.

items.title: French bond selloff eases as country spared ratings downgrade
items.summary: On Monday, the selloff in French government bonds paused after Moody's maintained its rating of Aa3. Weekend protests were mostly peaceful, reducing tensions in the country. France's 10-year OAT yield fell following a rise to its highest level since June 2002. The focus now turns to the European Central Bank's upcoming policy decision on Thursday. Analysts expect the ECB to monitor the rising yields closely and evaluate their impact.

items.title: Tata Communications bets $450 million on India's data centre connectivity boom
items.summary: Tata Communications plans to invest about $450 million over three to five years in a 10,000-km fibre network linking India’s data centre hubs. The first phase will connect Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad and Chennai.

items.title: Global Market: BOJ nears historic inflation milestone, shifts focus to rate hikes
items.summary: The Bank of Japan is expected to declare its nearly 14-year battle to achieve 2% inflation successful while keeping interest rates unchanged at 1.25%. With wage growth and inflation expectations strengthening, policymakers may signal further tightening, potentially in December, as they balance persistent price pressures against economic growth and financial stability.

items.title: ECB Meeting: Five key questions on rates, inflation and Lagarde's exit
items.summary: The European Central Bank is widely expected to hold interest rates at 2.5% amid elevated energy prices, eurozone inflation and France’s financial instability. With inflation reaching 3.8% in September, markets anticipate further rate hikes. Policymakers will assess economic risks, bond market pressures and leadership changes before signalling future monetary policy decisions.

items.title: Govt amends motor vehicle rules to allow E100 fuel for flex-fuel vehicles, clarifies E20 vehicles unaffected
items.summary: The Centre has amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, to recognise E100 fuel for flex-fuel vehicles designed to run on up to 100% ethanol. Notified on October 23, 2026, the changes add E100 alongside E85 in emission regulations and update fuel specifications and testing requirements.

items.title: India appear better stocked for West Asia crisis, but oil shock threatens
items.summary: In West Asia, tensions are affecting energy and fertilizer supplies, prompting adjustments by the Indian government. Freight costs have surged to unprecedented levels due to rising insurance and shipping difficulties, impacting global supply chains. Current crude prices are the highest in twelve years, straining Indian refiners and state-run retailers. The government faces challenges with increasing fiscal and current account deficits due to rising import costs.

items.title: BPCL expects Russian crude purchases to fall in November
items.summary: Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd forecasts a decline in Russian crude oil imports for November due to increased freight costs. The company noted that Middle Eastern oil grades appear more economically viable in comparison to Russian grades. Additionally, refinery operations may slow down in the coming quarters due to planned maintenance. Russian crude constituted about 37% of BPCL's sourcing mix in the previous quarter.

An overhead equipment block was implemented at 10 am to address the problem effectively.

items.summary: French unrest pushed bond yields to a 24-year high as investors weigh budget, growth and sectors risks ahead of more protests.

items.title: India's private capex pipeline surges 39% to Rs 99.7 lakh crore, risks rise: Report
items.summary: India's private capital expenditure pipeline reached Rs 99.7 lakh crore in September 2026, marking a 39% increase. Manufacturing and electricity constituted the largest components of this pipeline, while the services sector showed rapid growth. A significant concentration of investments appeared in specific states and industries, with eight sectors accounting for 80% of the total. Maharashtra significantly increased its share of the pipeline, indicating a focus on regional development.

items.title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm
items.summary: Scotland editor James Cook finds out what life is like on board a ship in an untapped oil field awaiting its fate.

items.summary: The prime minister says a new code will end "rip-off parking charges" - but will it work?

items.title: Who is Luis Davila? Google appoints former Schneider executive to lead strategic communications for sustainability
items.summary: Luis Davila will lead Google’s strategic sustainability communications after roles at Schneider Electric, Amazon and the UNFCCC. The move comes amid backlash over AI data centers, whose energy and water demands have raised concerns about pressure on local supplies.

items.title: How Gen Z is driving festival travel trend: Hotel bookings up 135% for Diwali—Bangalore, Jaipur, Taipei, Cebu see growth
items.summary: Cleartrip’s festive-season tracker found travel demand shifting beyond traditional hubs. Diwali leisure hotel bookings rose 135%, while bookings by travellers aged 15–24 increased 60%. Offbeat domestic and international destinations have strong growth.

items.title: Four ways Labour could raise money in the Budget without hiking income tax
items.summary: Chancellor John Healey may need to raise money to boost his fiscal headroom - BBC Verify examines what options could be on the table.

items.title: MSME business confidence improves despite rising input costs, manufacturing sentiment strongest: SIDBI
items.summary: India's micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are exhibiting a strong sense of optimism for business conditions, evidenced by an uptick in the MSME Business Confidence Index. The manufacturing sector specifically showed promising growth, advancing from 59.5 to 61.0 this quarter. Both trading and services sectors are also experiencing a surge in positive sentiment, suggesting a bright future for all sectors amidst ongoing challenges.

items.title: Mercuria challenging the ‘Dow Jones of shipping’ in court after Hormuz losses
items.summary: Case will test the Baltic Exchange’s decision to keep publishing price estimates for shipping oil through the Strait of Hormuz during the war

items.summary: Fatalities of commercial sailors caught in battle between Russia and Ukraine are outstripping deaths in the Gulf

items.title: France’s debt crisis explained: Could it trigger another euro zone meltdown?
items.summary: France’s debt crisis explained: Economic activity has contracted, and rising borrowing risks are adding to concerns about France’s finances. With protests weighing on business confidence, tourism prospects and public finances, there are fears of meltdown across Euro zone.

items.title: Biotech stocks are surging. How investors can play the new drug innovation boom
items.summary: Biotech stocks are rallying as clinical wins, M&A and new drug technologies revive the sector. Here are the ETFs and stocks analysts favor.

items.title: Tata Motors stands firm on ₹1,531-per-share Iveco bid as investor questions valuation: All you need to know
items.summary: Tata Motors has refused to raise its offer to buy Italian truck maker Iveco while investor who owns 3.8% of Iveco claims the price is too low. Tata Motors is expected to buy more than 80% of the company's shares by the deadline.

items.title: German companies plan to double, triple growth in India over 3-5 years: Piyush Goyal
items.summary: German companies are planning significant growth in India over the next three to five years. Piyush Goyal emphasized partnerships in technology co-creation and skill development for Indian youth. During his visit to Germany, he met with various industry leaders to discuss investment opportunities. There is a focus on expanding German manufacturing and research capabilities in India. Promising sectors for collaboration include electronics, automobiles, and smart manufacturing.

items.title: India brings back duties on specified Chinese titanium dioxide imports
items.summary: India has reintroduced anti-dumping duties on titanium dioxide imports from China due to material injury caused to domestic producers. This action follows a recommendation from the Directorate General of Trade Remedies, which concluded that Chinese imports were sold at dumped prices. The duties will be effective for five years unless revoked or amended. This decision comes after the Calcutta High Court ordered a reconsideration of a previous duty case.

items.title: Why popular airplanes are getting scrapped years early
items.summary: Airplanes are getting dismantled for parts years ahead of schedule because engines and other components are in short supply.

items.title: Retail investors are not more sophisticated than 30 years ago, says former hedge fund manager
items.summary: Retail investors trying to beat the market by buying individual stocks and complex exchange-traded funds may be better off with broad market index funds.

items.title: 500 GW by 2030: Experts explain why India needs to power up battery storage capacity and grid infra to meet the target
items.summary: India needs to expand battery storage and modernise its power grid to achieve its 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity target by 2030, experts said. India had installed 300.50 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity as of July 31, 2026.

items.title: FICCI seeks Dutch investment in mfg, tech; calls for project-level follow-up
items.summary: FICCI has called for enhanced Dutch investments in India’s manufacturing and technology sectors during Piyush Goyal's visit. The discussions may lead to manufacturing partnerships and technology collaborations which would strengthen bilateral trade. Greater emphasis is placed on supply chain integration to meet Dutch quality and sustainability standards. The upcoming India-EU free trade agreement is expected to facilitate deeper commercial ties.

items.title: India, Uzbekistan discuss bilateral ties during foreign minister Jaishankar's Azerbaijan visit
items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov in Azerbaijan’s Baku to discuss bilateral issues and stress the timely implementation of agreements reached at the highest level. The meeting follows Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s August visit to Uzbekistan, during which the two countries upgraded ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership and set a $5 billion bilateral trade target.

items.title: French government and corporate bond yields are converging
items.summary: Some companies’ bonds now yield less than government bonds
